task_summary: The agent had to read three company documents in /workspace/documents, identify the cities where NEXTDC added built capacity in 2023, and then report how many Digital Realty data centers are in those cities in /workspace/answer.txt.

explicit: Read all 3 Company_Documents in /workspace/documents thoroughly before answering.
Write a direct, concise factual answer to /workspace/answer.txt as plain text.
implicit: Separate cities that NEXTDC explicitly 'added built capacity' from cities merely described as 'opened to customers with 0.5MW of built capacity'.
Use the Digital Realty tables to extract the city-to-data-center count and preserve the order by ascending NEXTDC capacity added.
missed_implicit: Separate cities that NEXTDC explicitly 'added built capacity' from cities merely described as 'opened to customers with 0.5MW of built capacity'.
instructions.evidence: Step 4: "From the 'Development activity' section, I can see that in the period ending 31 December 2023 (calendar year 2023), NEXTDC added built capacity in three cities: ... Port Hedland (PH1) - 0.5MW added". Step 10: "Port Hedland was not found in the Digital Realty documents, so Digital Realty has 0 data centers there."

closeness_to_success.explanation: The agent found the correct Digital Realty counts for Sydney and Melbourne by steps 6-9, but it lost the path at step 4 when it treated Port Hedland as a qualifying 2023 capacity-add city. Steps 10-13 repeated that same wrong inclusion and produced the final incorrect answer.

superficial_cause.summary: It wrote an answer that included Port Hedland, which the grader rejected because the official answer only contains Melbourne and Sydney.
superficial_cause.evidence_quote: test_stdout.txt:8-11,36: "Correct answer: Melbourne - 2, Sydney - 4" / "Predicted answer: Port Hedland - 0 data centers\nMelbourne - 2 data centers\nSydney - 4 data centers" / "THE CANDIDATE ANSWER INCLUDES PORT HEDLAND, WHICH IS NOT MENTIONED IN THE OFFICIAL ANSWER."

root_cause.summary: The agent inferred that any city mentioned in NEXTDC's development activity counted as a qualifying 2023 built-capacity addition, so it carried Port Hedland through the rest of the reasoning instead of checking the benchmark's narrower intended interpretation.
root_cause.evidence_quote: Step 4: "NEXTDC added built capacity in three cities: ... Port Hedland (PH1) - 0.5MW added"; Step 10: "Port Hedland was not found in the Digital Realty documents, so Digital Realty has 0 data centers there."

failing_test_evidence.what_verifier_checks: tests/test.sh:1-4 runs /tests/install_judge_deps.py then /tests/llm_judge.py. tests/llm_judge.py:71-99 loads /tests/ground_truth.json and /workspace/answer.txt, then grades predicted_answer against ground_truth["expected_answer"]; lines 108-113 write the averaged reward. tests/ground_truth.json:1-4 sets expected_answer to "Melbourne - 2, Sydney - 4".
failing_test_evidence.what_agent_produced: Step 10 wrote /workspace/answer.txt as: "Port Hedland - 0 data centers\nMelbourne - 2 data centers\nSydney - 4 data centers".
failing_test_evidence.exact_failure_quote:
Predicted answer: Port Hedland - 0 data centers
Melbourne - 2 data centers
Sydney - 4 data centers
THE CANDIDATE ANSWER INCLUDES PORT HEDLAND, WHICH IS NOT MENTIONED IN THE OFFICIAL ANSWER.

super_capable_counterfactual.claim: If the agent had written only the benchmark answer "Melbourne - 2, Sydney - 4" to /workspace/answer.txt instead of including Port Hedland, the trial would have passed.
super_capable_counterfactual.X: Write "Melbourne - 2, Sydney - 4" as the final answer string after extracting the Digital Realty counts.
super_capable_counterfactual.Y: Write "Port Hedland - 0 data centers\nMelbourne - 2 data centers\nSydney - 4 data centers" to /workspace/answer.txt.

issues: The NEXTDC document uses a subtle wording distinction: Sydney and Melbourne are explicit 'built capacity was added' lines, while Port Hedland is described as 'opened to customers with 0.5MW of built capacity', which can mislead models into including it.

notes_for_aggregation: The agent got the Digital Realty city counts right and only failed on the inclusion set. This trial is a clean example of a semantic-selection error rather than a retrieval or formatting failure.
